results.evidence: Retry: the peak's only catalogued route elsewhere is the Northeast Ridge at 5.5 (4 pitches); the Mountaineers-style '5-pitch 5.5 Grade II' description is the peak's standard technical line, not a south route. The only south-face account still says the short exposed steps 'might have been low fifth class' with no number. No source grades a south route at 5.4 or 5.5. Would settle it: a guidebook or trip report that grades the south-side line.

results.evidence: Retry: the only figures found are for the Southern Pickets trip in general (just over 6,000 ft to Terror Basin camp; 20 mi and 10,000 ft for a full Pickets outing), not a car-to-car figure for the Chopping Block alone. No two sources state this route's total gain or loss. Would settle it: a trip report giving car-to-car gain for a Chopping Block-only trip.

USGS point elevations at the row's own pins: The Fin summit 5,597 ft (row 5,599 is correct), Flapjack Lakes 3,854 ft, so net camp-to-summit gain is ~1,750 ft and the straight-line distance is ~1 mi, making the itinerary's 2 mi day plausible and the waypoint distMi 10.5 (off-route Gladys Divide/Needle Pass line) the likely outlier. The only whole-trip figure (17 mi RT, 5,500 ft) still comes from one source; no second source states camp-to-summit distance or gain. Would settle it: a trip report giving Flapjack Lakes-to-Sawtooth Pass mileage/gain.

Retry: the grade table for The Fin Northeast Face lists '5.4 ... IV' where IV is the UIAA difficulty conversion, not an NCCS commitment grade, so the stored 'IV' is very likely a misread. Still no source states an NCCS commitment grade for The Fin. Would settle it: any guide or report giving a roman commitment grade for this tower.

Retry: a 2004 Sawtooth traverse party carried 2 ropes for the whole ridge but went round The Horn's east side and gives nothing on its rappel; route listings give only the 5.5 R grade. No source states the rappel length off The Horn or that two ropes are required for it. Would settle it: a Horn-specific description of the rappel length or rope requirement.

Retry: USGS point elevation at the Horn summit pin reads 5,535 ft (row 5,536 correct). The only outside total (17 mi RT, 5,500 ft) is the combined Fin & Horn figure from one source, repeated by search summaries of that same page; no independent second source was found. Would settle it: an independent trip report giving car-to-car gain for The Horn.

The emergency card itself says the peak is in Jefferson County and the Dungeness trailhead access in Clallam County; the Clallam sheriff serves the trailhead side and NPS dispatch, listed in the same field, is primary inside the park. By catalog convention, wrong-county sheriff findings that already carry NPS dispatch are refused rather than patched.
